title: Essential Phrasal Verbs
description: The most frequent and useful B2 phrasal verbs for everyday conversation, work and life.

items.definition: to refuse an offer or request; to make a sound or heat lower
items.example: She [turned down] the job offer because the salary was too low.
items.exampleRu: Она отказалась от предложения о работе, потому что зарплата была слишком низкой.
items.pattern: separable: turn it down / turn down the offer
items.trap: With a pronoun, the object must go in the middle: 'turn it down', not 'turn down it'.

items.definition: to think of an idea, plan or solution
items.example: Our team [came up with] a much cheaper way to ship the orders.
items.exampleRu: Наша команда придумала гораздо более дешёвый способ отправлять заказы.
items.pattern: inseparable: come up with it
items.trap: Don't drop 'with': 'come up with a plan', not 'come up a plan'.

items.definition: to understand something or find the answer to a problem after thinking
items.example: It took me an hour to [figure out] how the new coffee machine works.
items.exampleRu: Мне понадобился час, чтобы разобраться, как работает новая кофемашина.
items.pattern: separable: figure it out / figure out how/what/why...
items.trap: With a pronoun say 'figure it out', not 'figure out it'.

items.definition: to delay doing something until a later time
items.example: I keep [putting off] my dentist appointment because I hate needles.
items.exampleRu: Я всё откладываю визит к стоматологу, потому что терпеть не могу уколы.
items.pattern: separable: put it off / put off doing sth
items.trap: Followed by -ing, not 'to': 'put off calling', not 'put off to call'.

items.definition: to use all of something so that none is left
items.example: We [ran out of] milk, so I had my coffee black this morning.
items.exampleRu: У нас закончилось молоко, так что утром я пил чёрный кофе.
items.pattern: inseparable: sb runs out of sth; sth runs out (no 'of')
items.trap: Not 'The milk finished' or 'Milk is over' (calques of «молоко закончилось»). Say 'We ran out of milk' or 'The milk ran out'.

items.definition: to continue doing something
items.example: Sorry for interrupting, please [carry on] with what you were saying.
items.exampleRu: Извините, что перебил, продолжайте, пожалуйста.
items.pattern: intransitive: carry on doing sth / carry on with sth
items.trap: Use -ing or 'with': 'carry on working', not 'carry on to work'.

items.translation: в итоге оказаться, в конце концов (сделать)
items.definition: to finally be in a place or situation, often one you did not plan
items.example: We wanted to eat out, but we [ended up] ordering pizza at home.
items.exampleRu: Мы хотели поужинать в ресторане, но в итоге заказали пиццу домой.
items.pattern: intransitive: end up doing sth / end up in/with sth
items.trap: Followed by -ing, not 'to': 'ended up staying', not 'ended up to stay'.

items.definition: to get information about something or learn a fact
items.example: I only [found out] about the party when I saw the photos online.
items.exampleRu: Я узнал о вечеринке, только когда увидел фотографии в интернете.
items.pattern: find out (about sth) / find out that... / find out what/why...
items.trap: Use 'find out' (not 'know') for getting new information: 'I found out yesterday', not 'I knew yesterday'.

items.definition: to stop doing or having something, especially a habit
items.example: My dad finally [gave up] smoking after his doctor warned him.
items.exampleRu: Мой отец наконец бросил курить после предупреждения врача.
items.pattern: separable: give it up / give up doing sth
items.trap: Followed by -ing: 'give up smoking', not 'give up to smoke'.

items.definition: to feel happy and excited about something that is going to happen
items.example: I'm really [looking forward to] our holiday in Portugal next month.
items.exampleRu: Я с нетерпением жду нашего отпуска в Португалии в следующем месяце.
collocations: look forward to hearing from you
items.pattern: inseparable: look forward to sth / to doing sth
items.trap: 'To' is a preposition here: 'look forward to seeing you', not 'look forward to see you'.

items.definition: to examine a problem or situation to find out the facts
items.example: The bank promised to [look into] the strange payments on my account.
items.exampleRu: Банк пообещал разобраться со странными платежами на моём счёте.
items.pattern: inseparable: look into it
items.trap: It doesn't mean 'look inside': «заглянуть в коробку» is 'look in/inside the box'.

items.definition: to start talking about a subject; to care for a child until it is an adult
items.example: I didn't want to [bring up] money during our first dinner together.
items.exampleRu: Мне не хотелось заводить разговор о деньгах на нашем первом совместном ужине.
items.pattern: separable: bring it up / bring up the subject
items.trap: Not 'raise up' or 'lift' a topic (calques of «поднять тему»); say 'bring up a topic' or 'raise a topic'.

items.definition: to tell someone about a fact or problem they had not noticed
items.example: My colleague kindly [pointed out] a mistake in my report before the meeting.
items.exampleRu: Коллега любезно указал мне на ошибку в отчёте перед совещанием.
items.pattern: separable: point it out / point out that... / point sth out to sb
items.trap: Say 'point out sth to sb', not 'point sb out sth'.

items.definition: to start a business or organisation; to prepare equipment so it is ready to use
items.example: It took me all evening to [set up] the new Wi-Fi router.
items.exampleRu: Я весь вечер настраивал новый Wi-Fi роутер.
items.pattern: separable: set it up / set up a company
items.trap: «Настроить» a device or account is 'set up', not 'tune' ('tune' is for musical instruments, engines or radio stations). The noun is 'setup'.

items.definition: to start doing a new activity, especially for pleasure
items.example: After moving to the coast, she [took up] surfing at the age of forty.
items.exampleRu: Переехав на побережье, она в сорок лет занялась сёрфингом.
items.pattern: separable: take it up / take up doing sth
items.trap: Not 'I'm engaged in yoga' (calque of «занимаюсь»): 'engaged' usually means about to get married. 'Take up' = start; 'do' = practise ('I do yoga'). 'Take up time/space' = занимать.

items.definition: to happen in a particular way, or to be discovered to be true in the end
items.example: The restaurant looked expensive, but it [turned out] to be surprisingly cheap.
items.exampleRu: Ресторан выглядел дорогим, но оказался на удивление дешёвым.
items.pattern: intransitive: turn out to be sth / it turns out (that)...
items.trap: Don't translate «оказаться» as 'appear to be' when you mean the final result: 'It turned out that he was right'.

items.definition: to deal with a problem successfully or put things in order
items.example: Don't worry about the tickets — I'll [sort it out] tomorrow.
items.exampleRu: Не переживай из-за билетов, я завтра всё улажу.
items.pattern: separable: sort it out / sort out the problem
items.trap: It means «уладить», not «сортировать»; for putting items into groups use 'sort' or 'sort through'.

items.translation: справляться с, заниматься (проблемой), иметь дело с
items.definition: to take action to solve a problem or handle a situation or person
items.example: My manager is great at [dealing with] difficult customers on the phone.
items.exampleRu: Мой руководитель отлично справляется с трудными клиентами по телефону.
items.pattern: inseparable: deal with it / deal with sb
items.trap: Don't omit 'with': 'deal with the problem', not 'deal the problem'. Past form is 'dealt'.

items.definition: to feel better after an illness, a shock or something sad
items.example: It took him months to [get over] the break-up with his girlfriend.
items.exampleRu: Ему понадобились месяцы, чтобы пережить расставание с девушкой.
items.pattern: inseparable: get over it
items.trap: Not 'survive the break-up' for emotional recovery; 'get over' is the natural choice.

items.definition: to have a friendly relationship with someone
items.example: I [get along with] most of my neighbours, except the guy with the drums.
items.exampleRu: Я лажу с большинством соседей, кроме парня с барабанами.
items.pattern: inseparable: get along (with sb); British also 'get on (with sb)'
items.trap: Not 'find a common language' (calque of «найти общий язык»); say 'get along' or 'hit it off'.

items.translation: сломаться (о машине, технике); не выдержать, расплакаться
items.definition: to stop working (of a machine or car); to lose control of your emotions
items.example: Our car [broke down] on the motorway, and we waited two hours for help.
items.exampleRu: Наша машина сломалась на трассе, и мы два часа ждали помощи.
items.pattern: intransitive: sth breaks down
items.trap: Machines and cars 'break down'; a cup or a phone screen just 'breaks'. 'Break down sth' (separable) means split into parts: 'break down the costs'.

items.definition: to arrive somewhere, especially when expected or late
items.example: Only five people [showed up] to the meeting, so we rescheduled it.
items.exampleRu: На встречу пришли только пять человек, поэтому мы её перенесли.
items.pattern: intransitive: show up (at/to/for sth)
items.trap: Informal; in formal writing use 'arrive' or 'attend'.

items.definition: to experience a difficult situation; to examine something carefully
items.example: She's been [going through] a tough time since she lost her job.
items.exampleRu: С тех пор как она потеряла работу, у неё непростой период.
items.pattern: inseparable: go through it
items.trap: Not 'pass through difficulties'; say 'go through a difficult time'.

items.definition: to support someone or say that what they say is true; to copy computer files for safety
items.example: When I complained to the landlord, all my flatmates [backed me up].
items.exampleRu: Когда я пожаловался арендодателю, все соседи по квартире меня поддержали.
items.pattern: separable: back me up / back up your files
items.trap: With a pronoun the object goes in the middle: 'back me up', not 'back up me'.

items.definition: to use, eat or do less of something
items.example: I'm trying to [cut down on] coffee because I can't sleep at night.
items.exampleRu: Я стараюсь пить меньше кофе, потому что не могу спать по ночам.
items.pattern: inseparable: cut down on it
items.trap: Not 'reduce on coffee'; say 'cut down on coffee' or 'reduce my coffee intake'.

items.definition: to disappoint someone by not doing what they expected or trusted you to do
items.example: I felt really [let down] when my best friend missed my birthday dinner.
items.exampleRu: Я был очень разочарован, когда лучший друг не пришёл на мой праздничный ужин.
items.pattern: separable: let him down / feel let down
items.trap: Not 'bring sb down' (= make sb feel sad) or 'put sb down' (= criticise sb); «подвести» is 'let sb down'.

items.definition: (of a plane) to leave the ground; to suddenly become popular or successful
items.example: Her small online bakery really [took off] during the pandemic.
items.exampleRu: Её маленькая онлайн-пекарня по-настоящему пошла в гору во время пандемии.
items.pattern: intransitive: sth takes off; separable 'take sth off' = remove clothes
items.trap: Don't confuse with 'take sth off' (снять одежду): 'take off your shoes'.

items.definition: to wait for a short time (informal); to hold something tightly
items.example: Can you [hold on] a second? Someone's at the door.
items.exampleRu: Можешь подождать секунду? Кто-то звонит в дверь.
items.pattern: intransitive: hold on (a minute) / hold on to sth
items.trap: On the phone say 'Hold on' or 'Hang on', not 'Wait me'.

items.definition: to take someone or something to a place by car and leave them there
items.example: Could you [drop off] this parcel at the post office on your way?
items.exampleRu: Можешь завезти эту посылку на почту по дороге?
collocations: drop the kids off at school
drop sb off at the station
items.pattern: separable: drop me off / drop off the parcel
items.trap: Not 'throw me at the station' (calque of «закинь меня»); say 'drop me off at the station'.

items.definition: to meet someone you know by chance; to start to have problems
items.example: I [ran into] my old English teacher at the supermarket yesterday.
items.exampleRu: Вчера я случайно встретил в супермаркете свою бывшую учительницу английского.
items.pattern: inseparable: run into him / run into difficulties
items.trap: Not 'meet occasionally' («случайно» = 'by chance', 'occasionally' = «иногда»); say 'run into' or 'bump into'.

items.definition: to be very noticeable or much better than others
items.example: Her CV really [stood out] because of her volunteering experience abroad.
items.exampleRu: Её резюме сильно выделялось благодаря опыту волонтёрства за границей.
items.pattern: intransitive: stand out (from sth / as sth)
items.trap: Not 'stand out of the crowd'; the preposition is 'from'.

items.definition: to trust someone to help you or to do what they promise
items.example: You can always [count on] Anna to remember everyone's birthday.
items.exampleRu: На Анну всегда можно положиться: она помнит дни рождения всех.
collocations: count on sb to do sth
items.pattern: inseparable: count on sb (to do sth)
items.trap: Not 'calculate on sb' (from «рассчитывать на»): 'calculate' is only for numbers. Say 'count on' or 'rely on'.

items.definition: to take care of someone or something
items.example: My mum [looks after] our kids when we both work late.
items.exampleRu: Мама присматривает за нашими детьми, когда мы оба задерживаемся на работе.
items.pattern: inseparable: look after them
items.trap: Not 'look for' (искать) or 'look at' (смотреть на); «присматривать» is 'look after'.

items.definition: to accept an unpleasant situation or person without complaining
items.example: I can't [put up with] the noise from the building site much longer.
items.exampleRu: Я больше не могу терпеть шум со стройки.
items.pattern: inseparable: put up with it
items.trap: Not 'suffer the noise' or 'stand with'; say 'put up with' or 'can't stand'.

items.definition: to break into pieces because of being old or badly made; to fail completely
items.example: These cheap shoes [fell apart] after just two weeks.
items.exampleRu: Эти дешёвые туфли развалились всего через две недели.
items.pattern: intransitive: sth falls apart
items.trap: Not 'fall into pieces'; say 'fall apart' or 'fall to pieces'.

items.definition: to spend time doing something that you did not have time to do earlier
items.example: I'm going to spend the weekend [catching up on] sleep and emails.
items.exampleRu: Выходные я собираюсь потратить на то, чтобы отоспаться и разобрать почту.
items.pattern: inseparable: catch up on sth / on doing sth
items.trap: Don't confuse: 'catch up on sth' = do what you missed (sleep, work, news); 'catch up with sb' = reach sb, or meet and exchange news.

items.translation: не отставать от, успевать за, быть в курсе
items.definition: to move or progress at the same speed as someone or something
items.example: It's hard to [keep up with] all the new apps my kids use.
items.exampleRu: Трудно успевать за всеми новыми приложениями, которыми пользуются мои дети.
items.pattern: inseparable: keep up with it
items.trap: Don't confuse with 'catch up' (reach after being behind); 'keep up' = not fall behind.

items.definition: to do something good to repair a bad situation or a mistake
items.example: He bought her flowers to [make up for] forgetting their anniversary.
items.exampleRu: Он купил ей цветы, чтобы загладить вину за то, что забыл про годовщину.
items.pattern: inseparable: make up for sth / for doing sth
items.trap: Don't drop 'for': 'make up a story' means invent it; 'make up for a mistake' means compensate.

items.definition: to write the necessary information on a form or document
items.example: Please [fill in] this form and bring it to reception.
items.exampleRu: Пожалуйста, заполните эту анкету и принесите её на ресепшен.
items.pattern: separable: fill it in / fill in the form (US also 'fill out')
items.trap: Not just 'fill a form' (calque of «заполнить»); the particle is needed: 'fill in a form'.

items.definition: to start living a calm life in one place, often with a partner; to become calm
items.example: After years of travelling, they [settled down] in a small town near Lisbon.
items.exampleRu: После многих лет путешествий они осели в маленьком городке под Лиссабоном.
items.pattern: intransitive: settle down (in a place)
items.trap: Don't confuse with 'settle in' (привыкнуть к новому месту, освоиться).
